title: Inverse image preserves scalar matrices and their cokernels
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $R=\Lambda(*)$, and let $h:V\to U$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Use their small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], coefficient rings $\Lambda_U,\Lambda_V$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], canonical ring isomorphism $\alpha_h:h^{-1}\Lambda_U\cong\Lambda_V$ [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms], and module pullback $h^*$ [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. For $m,n\geq0$ and a matrix $A=(a_{ij})\in\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m}(R)$, let $A_U:\Lambda_U^m\to\Lambda_U^n$ and $A_V:\Lambda_V^m\to\Lambda_V^n$ act by the images of the same entries under the canonical scalar maps [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. Here finite free modules and cokernels use [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]. The regular-module comparison induced by $\alpha_h$, and its finite-coproduct extensions $e_r:h^*(\Lambda_U^r)\cong\Lambda_V^r$, satisfy $e_n\circ h^*(A_U)=A_V\circ e_m$. They induce an isomorphism $h^*\operatorname{coker}(A_U)\cong\operatorname{coker}(A_V)$ compatible with the cokernel projections.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-coefficient-diagram-regular-scalars] with $P=p_U^*$, $Q=p_V^*$, $F=h^{-1}$ and $c:Fp_U^*\cong p_V^*$. The pulled-back ring structures and the monoidal point-composition comparison give precisely this diagram; its component at $\Lambda$ is the ring isomorphism $\alpha_h$. Thus $R=\Lambda_U$, $T=h^{-1}\Lambda_U$, $S=\Lambda_V$ are commutative (for $T$ also use its ring isomorphism to $S$). Tensor on abelian sheaves preserves colimits and their abelian category has coequalizers, so the tensor hypotheses hold. A scalar $a\in\Lambda(*)$ is a map from the tensor unit to $\Lambda$; its transported sections are exactly the canonical scalar maps defining $A_U,A_V$. The lemma supplies the specified regular comparison $e_1$ and $e_1h^*(t_{a,U})=t_{a,V}e_1$ for every entry.

source.place: Monoidal point-composition comparison; the extracted coefficient-diagram lemma applied to the canonical scalar maps

proof.text: Write $H=h^*=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_h}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(h^{-1})$. Its module adjunction and [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] show that it preserves finite colimits. Only finite discrete indexing categories and the parallel-pair category are used. The module categories and their finite free objects are the abelian module categories of [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]. Consequently [lem-sfb-finite-colimit-matrix-cokernels] applies with $X=\Lambda_U$, $Y=\Lambda_V$ and the regular comparison from step 1. Its $E_r$ are the required finite-coproduct extensions $e_r$, including $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 0038, lemma-adjoint-exact (1); finite diagrams, then the extracted categorical comparison

proof.text: For each $i<n,j<m$, take $p_{ij}=t_{a_{ij},U}$ and $q_{ij}=t_{a_{ij},V}$. Step 1 supplies the entrywise-intertwining hypothesis of [lem-sfb-finite-colimit-matrix-cokernels]. By the definition of $A_U,A_V$ these are their entries. The lemma gives $e_nH(A_U)=A_Ve_m$ and the cokernel isomorphism $u$ with $uH(q_U)=q_Ve_n$. This is exactly the demanded projection compatibility. Its conclusion includes $m=0$, $n=0$ and both ranks zero.

lean.statement: theorem scalarMatrix_inverseImage {m n : ℕ} (A : Fin m → Fin n → (𝟙_ Ab.{u + 1} ⟶ scalarRingObj Λ)) : (CondensedRing.upperStar Λ h).map (scalarMatrix Λ U A) ≫ (scalarMatrixFreePullbackIso Λ h n).hom = (scalarMatrixFreePullbackIso Λ h m).hom ≫ scalarMatrix Λ V A ∧ ∃ e : (CondensedRing.upperStar Λ h).obj (cokernel (scalarMatrix Λ U A)) ≅ cokernel (scalarMatrix Λ V A), (CondensedRing.upperStar Λ h).map (cokernel.π (scalarMatrix Λ U A)) ≫ e.hom = (scalarMatrixFreePullbackIso Λ h n).hom ≫ cokernel.π (scalarMatrix Λ V A)
